Linux-only and tested on a single distro

Directory content depends on maintainer updates

Covers vendors, state agencies and data brokers in one place
risks: Coverage section is empty in the README digest

knowledge.description: Top Cyber Reconnaissance Threat Intelligence (Opensource)  Star if you like it!

risks: Mostly promotional framing with little concrete detail
Generic security list rather than focused OSINT curation
Tagline asks for stars, marketing-style content

media-forensics.description: Telegram chat exporter & backup tool: export chat history to HTML, JSON, and PDF, preserve observed edits and deletion notices, and share cryptographically signed archives. Self-hosted OSINT & digital forensics workspace.

Clear data sources and licence attribution
Working install path with an offline demo

Alpha status, with only one of ten real thunder cases located

Early version 0.2.0

Corroboration and conflict tracking with source attribution

Optional PII content scanning and sensitive-file discovery broaden scope

Dependency-free Python with a GUI and a terminal interface

risks: Metadata editing and stripping could be misused to scrub provenance
Version 1.0.0 with limited test coverage described in a separate doc

Names specific forensic techniques
risks: README is mostly marketing; little detail on limits or methods

Sample files and example output provided

Named decoders and bands with a clear install path
Passive reception of public transmissions

web-capture.summary: Chrome Manifest V3 extension that streams Wayback Machine CDX archived URLs, ranks them by security risk (.env, keys, .git, SQL dumps), mines parameters, verifies live 200s, and exports results.

Runs locally as an unpacked extension with clear install steps
Zero-tracking privacy stance stated
risks: Security-recon framing leans toward attack-surface work with bug-bounty and fuzzing emphasis
Some README claims are marketing-style (High-Performance, Zero Tracking badges)

web-capture.description: Ferramenta de dorking em múltiplos motores de busca para coleta de URLs em operações de OSINT e reconhecimento.
web-capture.summary: SimpleReconDorking runs search dorks in parallel across multiple search engines and returns the union of found URLs. Supports dork strings, files, a built-in categorised catalogue, and stdin, with Docker install and usage examples.
strengths: Clear purpose and multiple input modes
Documented usage examples and Docker setup
Built-in dork catalogue by category
risks: Dorking can be used to find exposed targets; README carries a consent warning only
Some engines require browser bypass, which may violate terms of service

web-capture.description: OSINT Gathering tool that accelerates your workflows.

Python codebase with a clear OSINT focus
risks: Student project, likely limited maintenance
README gives no features or data sources
Unclear what is collected, so legal and ethical impact is unknown

web-capture.description: OSINT time machine for the web: how a page looked, and what was removed from it.
web-capture.summary: Amber is a Windows web archive viewer that compares saved snapshots of a page side by side and marks removed text, changed prices, and removed people, with a count of removals over time.
strengths: Clear purpose focused on detecting deleted or changed web content
Side-by-side snapshot diff is a useful investigative approach
risks: README is mostly marketing and demo narrative with little on data sources or limits
Unclear which archive sources are used and how they are accessed

web-capture.summary: Python client that queries a CIRCL-hosted Common Crawl index service to search archived web pages by URL, hostname, FQDN or digest, and retrieves only the selected WARC byte ranges. Access requires a token issued by CIRCL on request.

Documents multiple search modes and output formats with examples
risks: Depends on a token-gated third-party service with discretionary access
Access controls and README sample commands are partially truncated

web-capture.description: Ferramenta de extração e descoberta de URLs para fluxos de OSINT e reconhecimento
web-capture.summary: Python CLI that takes seed URLs, fetches pages and passive/active sources to extract and discover reachable URLs, with optional same-origin spidering, recursive rounds, Docker support and API-key-based sources.
strengths: Clear purpose for URL discovery in recon workflows
Supports passive and active sources, crawling and Docker
Documents usage flags, profiles and presets
risks: Active probing of target sites may raise authorisation concerns
Readme digest shows template-like source examples, limited detail on data sources

web-capture.description: Find only verified and working Google dork commands, search operators and top dorks list for OSINT, bug bounty and site auditing.
web-capture.summary: A curated cheat sheet of Google search operators and dorks, grouped by whether Google documents or still supports them, with notes on removed operators. Includes a link to an interactive dork builder.
strengths: Clear grouping of documented versus undocumented operators
Notes on deprecated operators saves users time
risks: Reference document only, no executable tooling
Dork lists can be misused for finding exposed sensitive files

web-capture.summary: Python standard-library CLI that searches CourtListener's RECAP archive of federal court records, lists docket entries, and downloads free PDFs, with JSON output and token storage via Keychain or env var.
strengths: Single-file, standard-library-only Python tool
Clear command examples with inputs and outputs
Documents API limits and terms of use

workspace-analysis.description: Desktop OSINT tool that maps French companies, their directors and addresses into a sourced link graph, and flags patterns worth a closer look.
workspace-analysis.summary: Lacis is a Python/PySide6 desktop app that starts from a French company and pulls directors, addresses and BODACC notices from public open data into a sourced link graph, with explainable rules flagging patterns such as mass domiciliation or phoenix companies.

risks: Tracks directors and people across companies, which can enable personal profiling
Interface and docs are in French; 0.y version may change formats

Source preservation with SHA-256 hashes and Admiralty ratings
Named built-in collectors and graph analysis features
risks: Bundles username and email lookup tools that can profile individuals

workspace-analysis.description: Sherlock-compatible public username checks for DeepSeek Harness.
workspace-analysis.summary: Local temporal evidence workbench for DeepSeek Harness. It snapshots public URLs with SHA-256, records dated assertions across five clocks, flags deterministic date conflicts and gaps, and writes a local report. It does not issue verdicts or search for people.

Respects robots gate and per-host delay during ingestion
Explicit boundaries: no verdicts and no people search
risks: Name retained from a username-enumeration tool, which may confuse users
Legacy username tools section included in the same project
README digest is truncated, so some features are only partly verified

Clear architecture and stack documentation with CI and coverage badges

Not hardened for multi-tenant or production deployment

workspace-analysis.summary: A local investigator's desk over public Epstein court, DOJ and House Oversight records. Runs locally as a static binary over SQLite with FTS5
Documents provenance per item, file and PDF page

Source-available license rather than fully open source
Donation and social promotion elements in README

Honest limitations and status documentation
Local-first with no telemetry

Optional backends must be installed separately

workspace-analysis.summary: A local, offline investigation case tool for profiling subjects, mapping link networks with shortest path and centrality, placing locations on a map, building timelines, storing evidence with an audit log, and exporting PDF or HTML reports.

Install options and sample case reports provided

Tests and badges are self-reported; no independent verification of claims

Typed architecture with CLI and UI

Early-stage project with limited documented data sources
